work: Treatise On Subsidiary Points In Mourning Usages
heading: Liji 34 · Jian Zhuan 間傳 · Treatise On Subsidiary Points In Mourning Usages · Jian Zhuan 10

items.text: When mourning a father, keep the sackcloth with jagged edges as the most important; if a mother dies during that time, her lighter mourning is embraced in his, so do not change it.
items.quote: wearing of the sackcloth with jagged edges for a father... that which was most important was retained

items.text: Mourn your mother with the even-edged sackcloth for the prescribed period.
items.quote: the even-edged sackcloth for a mother

items.text: When you have the nine-month mourning for a relative, wear the sackcloth and grass-cloth bands together.
items.quote: both the sackcloth and grass-cloth bands were worn

work: Treatise On Subsidiary Points In Mourning Usages
heading: Liji 34 · Jian Zhuan 間傳 · Treatise On Subsidiary Points In Mourning Usages · Jian Zhuan 1 … Jian Zhuan 9

items.text: Fast for three days after your father's death.
items.quote: for a father, for three days he abstains from food

items.text: Fast for two days after your mother's death.
items.quote: for a mother, for two days

items.text: When wearing sackcloth for your father, hear what is said but do not reply in words.
items.quote: When wearing the sackcloth for a father, one indicates that he hears what is said to him, but does not reply in words

items.text: When wearing sackcloth for your mother, reply but do not speak of other matters.
items.quote: when wearing that for a mother, he replies, but does not speak of anything else

items.text: During mourning for a parent, live in the mourning shed on straw with a clod for your pillow, keeping headband and girdle; if for a mother only while your father is alive, live in the unplastered chamber on cut rushes.
items.quote: occupied the mourning shed, and slept on straw with a clod for his pillow, without taking off the headband or girdle

items.text: Eat only gruel at the coffining, and later only coarse rice and water, abstaining from vegetables and fruits until the prescribed sacrifices.
items.quote: take gruel made of a handful of rice in the morning, and the same quantity in the evening... eat coarse rice and drink water, but do not take vegetables or fruits

items.text: Present the sacrifice of repose after wailing ends, the smaller felicitous sacrifice at the year's end, the greater after another year, and the final sacrifice the following month.
items.quote: the sacrifice of repose has been presented
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; Christ is the only mediator (Lev 19:31; Deut 18:10-12; 1 Tim 2:5)

items.text: Modulate your wailing according to the degree of mourning: unbroken for a father, now and then broken for a mother.
items.quote: The wailing of one wearing the sackcloth for his father seems to go forth in one unbroken strain; that of one wearing the sackcloth for a mother is now and then broken
